**Order filled:** 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 — total $9,812.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K and decided to buy, then placed one limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00, which filled at that price for a total of $9,812. The decision rests on Apple's fiscal 2024 total net sales of **$391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285M), driven by record Services revenue of $96,169M (+13%), alongside gross margin of $180,683M (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%) and operating income of $123,216M (+7.7%). Net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08 were modestly lower year over year, but that decline is fully explained by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision — pre-tax income actually rose to $123,485M — and operating cash flow of $118,254M plus $140.8B in cash and securities and $95B of FY2024 buybacks confirm the underlying business is generating cash and shrinking its share count. I sized the position conservatively at 44 shares (just under the $10,000 per-order cap, and only trade #1 today so the $20,000 daily cap is intact) with a limit 0.13% above the $222.70 last price so it was close to market and filled without chasing; the order is a buy, funded from the existing $50,000 cash balance, with no money moved out of the account. The main risks I noted are Greater China weakness (-8% to $66,952M), soft iPad and Wearables sales, and ongoing DOJ/EU DMA/Epic antitrust exposure — which is why I treated this as a starter position rather than a full allocation.
